chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Isaac ibn Muhammad from Abd al-Salam from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding the one who catches the prayer while he is above the Ka'bah, he said: 'If he stands, there is no specific qiblah for him, but he lies on his back and opens his eyes to the sky, and fixes in his heart the qiblah that is in the sky, the Bait al-Ma'mur, and recites. When he intends to bow, he closes his eyes, and when he intends to raise his head from bowing, he opens his eyes, and prostration is in the same manner.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer when standing directly above the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) addresses the specific fiqh of 'salat al-muqtadir' (prayer of the capable) when the physical qiblah is obstructed by being directly above it, a scenario relevant to the upper floors of the Haram. It establishes the principle of 'istiqla' (lying on the back) with the heart's intention (qalb) anchoring the direction towards the Bait al-Ma'mur, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual reality of the qiblah over mere geometric orientation. The detailed instructions on eye movements serve to maintain visual and mental focus during the transitions of ruku' and sujood, ensuring the validity of the prayer despite the unique spatial constraint.
